name: Counterexample Persistence Audit
purpose: Verify that all formal proof attempts preserve previously identified counterexamples and failure boundaries.

mandatory_checks.note: Formal proof attempt (Section 5) explicitly identifies neighborhood instability as a boundary.
Formal proof attempt (Section 5) explicitly identifies orientation locking as a failure mode.
Formal proof attempt (Section 5) identifies non-reachable admissible states as a boundary.
Non-unique selection divergence is preserved as an exposure point.
Neighborhood stability requirement explicitly excludes divergent history.

governance_rules.rule: Every formal proof must pass the counterexample persistence audit before derivability classification.
Audit success does not imply that counterexamples have been 'solved', only that they remain visible.

forbidden_claims: Failure cases are irrelevant for local theorem work.
